text:
Anna (PM): ok folks — pulling together the PRD + acceptance criteria for the Optimize Toolkit (batching / caching / quant). need a short list of must-haves vs nice-to-haves and clear launch gates. Acme and HealthCo have pushed high-priority asks.
Mike (Eng-ML): +1. main technical constraints: model-agnostic recommendations only (can't assume kv-cache internals for every model), and quant guidance must include safety checks (quality regressions).
Tess (Eng-Platform): we also need to call out operator UX — one-click apply vs manual config. platform needs to expose experiment flags and rollback.
Sanjay (Eng Runtime): runtime concerns: continuous batching impacts tail latency. we should require gold-standard latency SLOs per workload and a fallback path (single-request mode) when latency breaches.
Julia (Solutions): from customers: they want deterministic cost forecasts and a short checklist to validate in staging before prod. HealthCo specifically asked for on-prem guidance for HSM/KMS interactions.
Ben (Eng-ML): propose acceptance criteria draft: 1) recommendations reduce token cost by >= 15% on representative workloads without quality drop > 3% (measured by eval set) 2) has opt-out per-route 3) rollout can be canaryed to 5% users and auto rollback on metric regression.
Lisa (Design): add simple UX flows for "Apply recommendations" and "Preview impact". the preview should show sample prompt token delta and expected latency change.
Anna (PM): good. trying to distill into the PRD gating matrix. posting current draft below — please flag anything missing.
Anna (PM): ```yaml
gates:
  - name: safety-quality-check
    must_have: true
    checks:
      - evaluation_suite_run: true
      - max_quality_regression_pct: 3
  - name: latency-slo
    must_have: true
    checks:
      - p95_latency_change_pct: 10
      - fallback_path_verified: true
  - name: cost-benefit
    must_have: true
    checks:
      - expected_unit_cost_reduction_pct: 15
      - break_even_months: 2
  - name: onprem-compliance
    must_have: conditional
    checks:
      - kms_integration_docs: provided
      - airgapped_test_plan: provided
```
Mike (Eng-ML): looks good. a few edgecases to call out inline: 1) quantization-induced token-level distribution shifts — we should require a small sample of prompts for log-prob drift checks 2) caching prefix mismatch: if cached prefix diverges, app must detect and invalidate gracefully 3) batching + streaming — ensure streaming clients don't stall behind batch window.
Sanjay (Eng Runtime): adding to edgecases: - warmup penalties when enabling batching on cold nodes - KV cache TTLs and eviction races across replicas - memory fragmentation for quantized kernels (esp int8 jit paths)
Anna (PM): noted. adding acceptance bullet for log-prob drift and graceful cache invalidation.
Ben (Eng-ML): propose simple tests we can include in PRD: - regression test harness that runs N=500 prompts across small/medium/large seq lengths and reports: perplexity delta, token-accuracy delta, latency percentiles. - run with quantized model and fp16 baseline.
Julia (Solutions): also add a customer-facing checklist: staging run, sample prompts from prod, compare top-1 output diff rate, validate billing model on a shadow run.
Tess (Eng-Platform): on rollout mechanics: need API for "recommendation set" that can be attached to a route. API should support: preview, dry-run (shadow), apply, rollback. minimal config example: ```json
{
  "route": "/chat",
  "recommendations": {
    "batch_window_ms": 10,
    "kv_cache_ttl_sec": 3600,
    "quant_profile": "int8-safe"
  }
}
```
Lisa (Design): question: for the preview UI, do we show per-prompt outputs side-by-side or just metrics? customers asked for both in interviews.
Anna (PM): both — metrics first, then expand to side-by-side diff for a handful of sampled prompts. keep it limited to 10 examples to avoid overwhelm.
Mike (Eng-ML): about quant_profile: we should ship 2 starter profiles: "int8-safe" (aggressive size reduction, conservative on certain ops), and "int8-aggressive" (more compression, higher risk). require explicit acceptance for aggressive.
Sanjay (Eng Runtime): and runtime should enforce a fail-safe: if downstream eval signals > threshold regression, automatically revert all routes with that profile.
Ben (Eng-ML): example acceptance criteria text we can paste into PRD: "Quantization recommendations must include a documented validation run demonstrating that model outputs on the customer-provided eval set have a maximum degradation of 3% on primary metrics AND no hierarchical safety violation."
Julia (Solutions): safety violation == hallucination increase or policy trigger count increase? define it.
Anna (PM): yep will define in safety appendix: policy triggers, hallucination flags from eval harness, and manual review threshold.
Tess (Eng-Platform): ops note: we need telemetry + tracing hooks to tie recommendations to cost/latency/quality signals. add a requirement: per-route attribution and tracing id in logs.
Anna (PM): adding that as must-have.
Lisa (Design): small UX ask: add a "why this recommendation" tooltip that shows rationale (batching reduces per-token overhead by X%, cache avoids repeated prompt tokenization, quant reduces mem footprint).
Ben (Eng-ML): Also include a rollback plan doc snippet. quick snippet: ```text
Rollback plan:
- Detect regression -> set route to baseline profile -> monitor for 15m -> if stable, mark incident resolved.
- Notify customer and SE owner with diff report.
```
deploy-bot: "deployment scheduled: optkit/rfc-draft -> staging at 2026-04-12T21:00:00Z"
Anna (PM): action items: @Mike to draft evaluation harness steps, @Tess to spec API endpoints and telemetry, @Sanjay to list runtime fail-safes, @Julia to draft customer staging checklist, @Lisa to wireframe preview UI. we'll reconvene Thursday for PRD sign-off.
Mike (Eng-ML): on it. expect a first-pass by Wed EOD.
Tess (Eng-Platform): I'll post API proto + example by Wed.
Sanjay (Eng Runtime): will list runtime tests + chaos scenarios.
Julia (Solutions): collecting customer prompts this week.
Anna (PM): thanks — great start. tagging this thread as the canonical PRD draft conversation. feel free to add inline edits to the doc in google drive. :thumbsup:
